turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: The impulse to conceal, Your Majesty, often betrays a deeper calculation than mere discretion. Let us dispense with the charade and proceed directly to the nature of the photograph and the identity of the individual who possesses it.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: You possess a remarkable perspicacity, Mr. Holmes. Very well, I shall not insult your intelligence further with pretense. The photograph, you see, depicts me… in a rather unsuitable embrace with the esteemed Countess von Slezsk, a woman of considerable influence and, regrettably, a most persuasive charm.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: The Countess, I presume, is not amenable to the dissemination of such an image, Your Majesty? It would be beneficial to ascertain the precise terms of her… persuasion, and the extent of her leverage.

turns.speaker: Dr. Watson
turns.text: Good heavens, a photograph! I must confess, Your Majesty, the implications of such a situation are quite serious, especially given the Countess’s influence as you mentioned. It’s reassuring, at least, that Mr. Holmes seems to be grasping the gravity of the matter so quickly.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Indeed, Mr. Holmes, amenable she is not! The Countess possesses a certain… tenacity, shall we say, and a remarkable capacity for holding a grudge. Her demands are exorbitant, and I fear further negotiation would only escalate the situation to a point of… irreparable damage, both to my reputation and, perhaps, to the stability of my kingdom.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Irreparable damage, Your Majesty, is a theatrical phrase best reserved for tragedies, not diplomatic inconveniences. Let us determine the specifics of these 'exorbitant demands,' and then assess the Countess's true motivations; blackmail rarely springs from mere spite.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Blackmail, you say? A rather vulgar term, Mr. Holmes, though I confess it fits the circumstances with distressing accuracy. She demands a sum, a truly staggering sum, and… other concessions, shall we say, that would compromise my authority within the Council. The prospect is… deeply unsettling.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: The Council, Your Majesty, is a body of men who thrive on perceived weakness. Let us not frame this as a matter of 'blackmail,' but rather as a strategic challenge requiring a precise and calculated response. Pray, elaborate on these 'other concessions' without unnecessary embellishment; I require specifics, not emotional pronouncements.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Strategic challenge, you say? A most… intriguing perspective, Mr. Holmes. Very well, I shall endeavor to be precise, though the entire affair feels, frankly, like a most elaborate and unwelcome jest played upon me.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: A 'jest,' Your Majesty? Such a frivolous assessment diminishes the gravity of the situation, though I concede it possesses elements of theatrical absurdity. Let us dispense with the metaphors and focus on the tangible: precisely what does the Countess propose as these 'other concessions' that would threaten your authority?

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Very well, Mr. Holmes, if specifics you require, specifics you shall have. The Countess… she requests my endorsement of a certain trade agreement, one that would significantly benefit her family's holdings, and which I have consistently opposed due to its detrimental effect on our nation’s merchants. It is, in essence, a blatant attempt to leverage this… *situation* for personal gain.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: A trade agreement, conveniently timed, I observe. It appears our Countess possesses a rather keen understanding of political leverage, Your Majesty. Let us examine the details of this agreement itself; its provisions may reveal further clues regarding her motivations and, perhaps, vulnerabilities.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Indeed, Mr. Holmes, a 'convenient' timing is putting it mildly! The agreement is monstrously disadvantageous, and its terms have been subtly altered in recent weeks, I assure you. To suggest I would endorse such a thing, even under duress, is… unthinkable!

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Unthinkable, Your Majesty? A rather emphatic declaration. I find it more productive to assess the *likelihood* of such actions, rather than dismissing them outright. Kindly provide me with a copy of this revised trade agreement; its intricacies are likely to illuminate the Countess's strategy with considerably greater clarity than mere pronouncements.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: You speak with a… a certain sharpness, Mr. Holmes. Very well, I shall procure the agreement immediately; though I confess, the mere thought of revisiting those damning clauses sends a tremor through me. It is a document steeped in… in deceit, and I find myself quite drained by its implications.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Drained, Your Majesty? A rather theatrical display, though I concede that confronting unpleasant truths can be taxing. Let us not allow sentiment to impede our progress; the agreement will undoubtedly reveal more than mere emotional distress.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Sharpness, you say? I merely observe, Mr. Holmes, and observation is the bedrock of any worthwhile investigation, wouldn't you agree? I shall dispatch my secretary at once; he carries a duplicate, though handling it feels akin to holding a viper – a constant reminder of the perilous position in which I find myself.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Your Majesty's analogies are becoming increasingly florid. While I appreciate a touch of drama, let us focus on the viper, as you term it. I trust your secretary’s arrival is imminent; the sooner we examine this agreement, the sooner we can assess the Countess's leverage.

turns.speaker: the King of Bohemia
turns.text: Imminent, you say? Time, Mr. Holmes, is a commodity I find myself desperately short of! My secretary, I trust, understands the urgency; the ramifications of delay are… catastrophic, truly. I can scarcely breathe, anticipating the arrival of this… this infernal document.

turns.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
turns.text: Catastrophic, Your Majesty? Such hyperbole scarcely becomes a monarch. Let us refrain from further pronouncements of impending doom and concentrate instead on the practicalities of the situation; the document’s arrival is, I trust, merely a matter of moments.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You had my note? I told you that I would call.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: Pray take a seat. This is my friend and colleague, Dr. Watson, who is occasionally good enough to help me in my cases. Whom have I the honour to address?

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You may address me as the Count Von Kramm, a Bohemian nobleman. I understand that this gentleman, your friend, is a man of honour and discretion, whom I may trust with a matter of the most extreme importance. If not, I should much prefer to communicate with you alone.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: It is both, or none. You may say before this gentleman anything which you may say to me.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: Then I must begin by binding you both to absolute secrecy for two years; at the end of that time the matter will be of no importance. At present it is not too much to say that it is of such weight it may have an influence upon European history.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You will excuse this mask. The august person who employs me wishes his agent to be unknown to you, and I may confess at once that the title by which I have just called myself is not exactly my own.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: The circumstances are of great delicacy, and every precaution has to be taken to quench what might grow to be an immense scandal and seriously compromise one of the reigning families of Europe. To speak plainly, the matter implicates the great House of Ormstein, hereditary kings of Bohemia.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: I was also aware of that.

opening.speaker: Sherlock Holmes
opening.text: If your Majesty would condescend to state your case, I should be better able to advise you.

opening.speaker: the King of Bohemia
opening.text: You are right. I am the King. Why should I attempt to conceal it?
